extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, peer reviewers, authors of healthcare research, and clinicians/consumers of research
extracted.subtask_description: Recommendations and evaluative criteria for detecting and preventing 'spin' (misleading presentation of results) in scientific articles, especially abstracts and press releases, aimed at improving transparency and research integrity in healthcare journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of spin
rubrics_metrics.description: Spin is an overenthusiastic and often misleading presentation of the results of a study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spin can distort readers' ability to interpret results independently and create false hope for patients if clinicians accept conclusions at face value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locations where spin can appear
rubrics_metrics.description: Spin can appear in the title, abstract or in the full text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial checks should cover all parts of the manuscript (title, abstract, full text) because misleading statements may be present in any section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation or title suggesting positive effect inconsistent with findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract recommendations of an intervention, or titles suggesting a positive effect, that are not consistent with the study findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag any recommendation or positive framing when primary results do not support such claims; the editorial team should ensure consistency between conclusions and actual findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selective reporting of outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Selective reporting of positive and negative outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that both favorable and unfavorable outcomes are reported; check that emphasis in the abstract matches the pre-specified primary outcomes and full-text reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming safety based on non-statistically significant results
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements asserting safety (or efficacy) based on non-statistically significant results for primary outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not interpret non-significance as evidence of no effect/safety; editors/reviewers should correct overstated safety claims that are not supported by statistical evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selective reporting of harm outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Selective reporting (or omission) of adverse events or harms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Harm outcomes must be transparently reported and not downplayed; check abstracts and full text for consistent harm reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overstating conclusions to other interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclusions that are overstated or generalized to other interventions beyond the study scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that conclusions are restricted to the interventions and populations actually studied; prevent inappropriate generalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press releases and news coverage can propagate spin
rubrics_metrics.description: Misleading messages can be disseminated by press releases and news coverage, amplifying spin from articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journal policies should consider the role of press releases and encourage accurate, non-exaggerated communication to media; watch for exaggeration originating in academic press releases (cited evidence of association).

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility to provide transparent information
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors, journal editors and reviewers have the obligation to provide adequately, consistent and transparent information and to follow research codes of conduct and ethical principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial processes should enforce research integrity standards (e.g., Declaration of Helsinki) and ethical principles to reduce misleading reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory use of reporting guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandatory use of reporting guidelines, not only for full text but also for abstracts, highlighted as one of the 'instructions for authors'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include PRISMA for Abstracts and CONSORT for abstracts; require authors to follow appropriate checklists when submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check adherence to reporting guidelines and abstract–full text consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Proper checking if authors have followed the adequate reporting guidelines for abstracts and full text, checking also for abstracts' consistency of reporting and interpretation with the full text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial staff/reviewers should verify that abstracts accurately reflect results and interpretation presented in the full text and that reporting checklists are completed correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness and detection of spin
rubrics_metrics.description: Awareness of spin in the abstracts and full texts, with adequate interpretation of results and conclusions of trials and reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors and reviewers should be trained to identify common spin types and correct overstated or inconsistent interpretations during peer review and editing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility with abstract word count
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow more flexibility with the abstract word count.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rigid word limits may encourage omission or selective reporting; increased allowance can enable fuller, more balanced reporting of primary outcomes and harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intensive training for editors and reviewers about spin
rubrics_metrics.description: Intensive training for journal editors and reviewers with regard to spin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide training programs so editorial teams can detect and prevent spin, and enforce consistent interpretation of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advice for consumers: do not rely only on abstracts; learn critical appraisal
rubrics_metrics.description: Consumers of research should not rely only upon abstracts for decision making and should read and interpret the corresponding full texts by themselves; critical appraisal skills training is urgently needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clinicians and other stakeholders should be encouraged to read full reports and receive training in critical appraisal to avoid being misled by spun abstracts or press coverage.
